Let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ be a random sample of size $n$ from a uniform distribution on the interval $(\alpha-\beta,\, \alpha+\beta)$, where $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\beta>0$ are unknown parameters.

(a) Derive the method of moments estimators of $\alpha$ and $\beta$.
(b) A random sample of five observations from such a population is $5,\,3,\,1,\,4,\,2$. Compute the method of moments estimates of $\alpha$ and $\beta$.

Let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ be a random sample from a geometric distribution with probability mass function

$$
f(x, p) =
\begin{cases}
p(1-p)^{x-1}, & x = 1, 2, 3, \dots \\
0, & \text{elsewhere}
\end{cases}
$$

where $0 < p < 1$ is an unknown parameter.

(a) Obtain the maximum likelihood estimator of $p$.
(b) Suppose a random sample of size $3$ is taken with $x_1 = 3$, $x_2 = 7$, and $x_3 = 8$. Calculate the maximum likelihood estimate of $p$.

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be independent exponential observations with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta) =
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{\theta} e^{-x/\theta}, & x > 0, 
0, & \text{elsewhere},
\end{cases}
$$

where $\theta > 0$ is an unknown parameter.

(i) Show that $\bar{X}$ is an unbiased estimator of $\theta$. (5 marks)
(ii) State the Cramér–Rao lower bound for an unbiased estimator of $\theta$. (2 marks)
(iii) Obtain the Cramér–Rao lower bound for an unbiased estimator of $\theta$. (6 marks)
(iv) Show that $\bar{X}$ is a minimum variance unbiased estimator (MVUE) of $\theta$. (7 marks)

A random sample of 10 children from a certain population was taken and their weights (in kg) were recorded. The sample mean weight was found to be \(38.4\text{ kg}\). Assume that the population of weights is normally distributed with unknown mean \(\mu\) and known variance \(\sigma^2 = 30\text{ kg}^2\). Construct a \(98\%\) confidence interval for the population mean weight \(\mu\).

Let $X$ be a continuous random variable with probability density function

$$
f(x)=\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{\theta}, & 0\le x\le \theta,
0, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
$$

where $\theta>0$ is an unknown parameter. Let $X_1,X_2,\dots,X_n$ be a random sample of size $n$ from this distribution, and let $\bar X=\dfrac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ be an estimator of $\theta$.

(a) Find
 

(i) $E(\bar X)$; **(5 marks)**
(ii) $\operatorname{Var}(\bar X)$. **(11 marks)**
(b) Is $\bar X$ an unbiased estimator of $\theta$? Justify your answer. **(1 mark)**
(c) Is $\bar X$ a consistent estimator of $\theta$? Justify your answer. **(3 marks)**

A random sample of size three, \(x_1 = 0.4,\; x_2 = 0.7,\; x_3 = 0.9\), is taken from a continuous distribution with probability density function

$$
f(x) =
\begin{cases}
\theta x^{\theta-1}, & 0 \le x \le 1, \\
0, & \text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
$$

where \(\theta > 0\) is an unknown parameter. Estimate \(\theta\) by the method of

(a) Moments (10 marks)
(b) Maximum likelihood estimation (10 marks)

Let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ be a random sample of size $n$ from a Poisson distribution with probability mass function

$$
f(x;\lambda)=\frac{e^{-\lambda}\lambda^x}{x!},\qquad x=0,1,2,\dots,\ \lambda>0.
$$

(a) Find the Fisher information $I(\lambda)$ contained in a single observation, and hence state the Cramér–Rao lower bound for the variance of any unbiased estimator of $\lambda$ based on the sample. (6 marks)
(b) Show that $T=\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i$ is a sufficient statistic for $\lambda$, and explain why $T$ is also complete. (5 marks)
(c) Using the fact that $T\sim \mathrm{Poisson}(n\lambda)$, show that $\bar X=T/n$ is an unbiased estimator of $\lambda$ and that its variance attains the Cramér–Rao lower bound. Hence state the minimum variance unbiased estimator (MVUE) of $\lambda$. (5 marks)
(d) State the necessary and sufficient condition, in terms of the likelihood function, for an unbiased estimator to be an MVUE, and verify that $\bar X$ satisfies this condition. (4 marks)

Let $X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_n$ be a random sample from a normal population with mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2$, where both $\mu$ and $\sigma^2$ are unknown.

(a) State what it means for an estimator $\hat{\theta}$ of a parameter $\theta$ to be unbiased. **(2 marks)**
(b) Show that $\bar{X} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ is an unbiased estimator of $\mu$. **(3 marks)**
(c) Derive the Cram\'{e}r--Rao lower bound for unbiased estimators of $\mu$ in this model, and hence show that the variance of $\bar{X}$ attains this lower bound. **(10 marks)**
(d) Show that $\bar{X}$ is a consistent estimator of $\mu$. **(5 marks)**

A random sample of 12 fuel rods from a production process is tested, and the percentage of enrichment is measured. The summary statistics are 

$$
\sum_{i=1}^{12} x_i = 34.82, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{12} x_i^2 = 101.1486.
$$

 Assume that the percentage of enrichment is normally distributed with unknown mean \(\mu\) and unknown variance \(\sigma^2\).

(a) Compute the sample mean and the sample variance. (4 marks)
(b) Construct a \(99\%\) confidence interval for the population mean percentage of enrichment \(\mu\). Interpret your interval. (8 marks)
(c) Construct a \(95\%\) confidence interval for the population variance \(\sigma^2\). (8 marks)

Let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ be a random sample of size $n$ from a population with probability density function $f(x, \theta)$, where $\theta$ is an unknown parameter. Let $T = t(X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n)$ be an unbiased estimator of a function $\psi(\theta)$. State the regularity conditions required and derive the Cramer-Rao Inequality (CRI). Hence, let $X_1, X_2, \dots, X_n$ be a random sample from a Poisson distribution with probability mass function

$$
f(x, \lambda) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^x}{x!}, & x = 0, 1, 2, \dots, \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere}, \end{cases}
$$

where $\lambda > 0$ is unknown.

(i) Obtain the minimum variance unbiased estimator (MVUE) of $\lambda$ and its variance.
(ii) Obtain the Cramer-Rao lower bound for $e^{-\lambda}$.

A random sample of 18 components produced by Machine A gave a sample mean lifetime of $\bar{x}_1 = 1250$ hours with sample variance $s_1^2 = 1600$. An independent random sample of 22 components produced by Machine B gave a sample mean lifetime of $\bar{x}_2 = 1210$ hours with sample variance $s_2^2 = 2500$. Assume that the lifetimes from both machines are normally distributed with a common (unknown) variance. Construct a 95\% confidence interval for the difference between the true mean lifetimes, $\mu_1 - \mu_2$.

A study compares the lifespan (in days) of two independent populations of mosquitoes: wild type and transgenic. Two independent random samples are taken, and the summary statistics are given below.

| Population | Sample size | Sample mean | Sample standard deviation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wild type | $n_1 = 80$ | $\bar{x}_1 = 20.78$ | $s_1 = 12.99$ |
| Transgenic | $n_2 = 90$ | $\bar{x}_2 = 16.54$ | $s_2 = 10.78$ |

Assuming that the two populations are normally distributed with a common but unknown variance, construct a $95\%$ confidence interval for the difference between the population means $\mu_1 - \mu_2$, where $\mu_1$ is the mean lifespan of wild type mosquitoes and $\mu_2$ is the mean lifespan of transgenic mosquitoes. Interpret your interval.
